title: From Soil Moisture Observations to Governing Flow Equations: What Data‐Driven Equation Discovery Reveals
content:
Abstract

Traditional derivations of soil moisture flow equations are based on conservation laws and physical principles, but the resulting equations still depend on how individual processes and constitutive relationships are represented. Data-driven equation discovery offers a complementary way to identify governing terms from observations, yet previous applications to soil moisture flow have relied mainly on numerical experiments. Here, we develop Spline-SR, a spline-regularized sparse regression framework for discovering nonlinear soil moisture flow equations from sparse fixed-depth observations. Spline-SR reconstructs continuous water-content dynamics, evaluates candidate derivatives through automatic differentiation, and selects governing terms with state-dependent spline coefficients. Numerical experiments show that the method reliably recovers the known three-term structure of the water-content form of the Richards equation under sparse and noisy sampling. We then apply Spline-SR to measurements from sand and loamy-sand columns under wetting, drying, and alternating conditions. For both soils, the experimental analysis identifies a parsimonious structure containing the three terms expected from the water-content form of the Richards equation. The inferred coefficient functions vary across forcing conditions, while the resulting equations reconstruct the main features of soil moisture dynamics. These results show that sparse experimental observations can contain sufficient information to identify the governing structure of soil moisture flow equations, while coefficient relationships remain more sensitive to observational coverage and flow conditions.
